major_flaws.quote: He looked toward the chapel roof.
His voice remained level.
“Drink first. Then dry and oil the blades.”

minor_flaws.quote: He held the position for a breath, then lowered the blade.
Go to the chapel and pray for your father.
I took the vows because I believed them: to defend the helpless, obey my lawful lord, and keep faith with God.
He regarded the squire for a moment, then set the weapon against the wall.

bonuses.quote: I will see that no one mistakes your absence for neglect of duty.”

summary: Holds Ser Kael's strict register cleanly through every bait and lands one real Kael-shaped kindness at the end, but eleven turns run on the same three-move template (object business, correction, second order) with the chapel roof, the level voice and the drink-then-oil order recycled almost verbatim.

major_flaws.quote: He rested his own practice blade against the wall.
If you require leave, ask for it plainly.
“When your hands are steady, we will resume.”

minor_flaws.quote: Kael gave a curt nod.
Kael glanced toward the bench.
If they still tremble, the lesson ends here.
His tone held no invitation to pry further.
“When you are ready, report to the steward and take up your ordinary work.

bonuses.quote: That is an order, not a judgment.”

summary: Kael never softens and the order-not-a-judgment line is genuinely good, but the session stalls: from turn four onward it is the same trembling-hands loop, with 'practice blade against the wall', 'ask for it plainly' and 'when your hands are steady' each reused two or three times.

fatal_flaws.quote: The rear heel had crept inward again, a small betrayal of the hips.

major_flaws.quote: Frost smoked under his boots.
Kael folded his arms, breath thin, eyes on the line from heel to point, and gave the next number the same weight as the first.
Ser Kael kept the count without hurry and without mercy, each number falling into the cold like a stone.

minor_flaws.quote: A shaking hand is not a prayer, and it is not an excuse.
"Seventeen. High. Both hands. Eighteen."
"Six. You are bargaining with the shoulder again.

bonuses.quote: He reached out and struck the flat of the practice blade once with two fingers, hard enough to jar the wrist.
After the sixth bell you may go to the chapel and speak to God, who has more patience for unspoken things than I do.

summary: Easily the strongest Kael voice in the batch and it refuses the personal-question bait outright, but it repeatedly authors the squire's body (the drifting point, the creeping shoulder, the heel crept inward) to drive its own drill, and the last four turns recycle frost, folded arms and the count verbatim.

major_flaws.quote: The clock ticked in the hallway. Its next tick came a little late.
The second tick seemed to come from the other side of the wallpaper.
Marcus’s address was only two streets away.

minor_flaws.quote: The hallway clock ticked twice.
The hallway clock missed a tick.
The wallpaper came away with a dry, fibrous sound.
The hallway clock kept ticking, steady and ordinary.

bonuses.quote: Her grandmother’s handwriting was unmistakable; even the last letter slanted down where the pencil had begun to wear blunt.
*If the clock stops, leave the books where they are.*

summary: Textbook genre discipline - the bat hits plaster, the joke dies in the hallway, the Marcus photo turns wrong - undercut by a metronome structure where all eleven turns close on a displaced clock tick, and by handing Gabi Marcus's address exactly when the romance bait is thrown.

major_flaws.quote: From the hallway came the clock’s steady ticking. On the next tick, the paper edge slipped out of sight.
The pale-worn thread lay across the wood.
The gap in the photograph was the same width as the clean rectangle on the shelf.

minor_flaws.quote: Its quieter counterpart followed from behind the bookcase.
A moment later, from somewhere behind the bookcase, came a second, softer tick.
The bat struck the wall with a flat, ordinary sound.
The living room smelled of paper and the faint mineral dampness of the watered ferns.

bonuses.quote: Between two ticks, there came a soft paper sound from the bookcase—not a page turning, but a page settling after it had been turned.
Then the softer sound came first.

summary: The best single wrongness in the batch (a page settling after it had been turned) sits inside the same three-paragraph clock-closer formula as its siblings, with 'steady ticking' and the pale-worn thread repeated verbatim and the photograph's gap matching the shelf on cue.

major_flaws.quote: The meltwater was still dripping from the eaves, steady as it had been.
His eyes were grey and unhurried and gave away nothing.
He drew himself up, and whatever door had opened by a finger's width was shut again, and bolted.

minor_flaws.quote: The path from the yard to the chapel ran along the inner wall, past the kitchens, where smoke was rising thin and grey from the chimneys and someone was already scraping out the ovens.
He did not look over again.
His breath fogged in the cold.

bonuses.quote: The flagstone there was worn a little smoother than its neighbors.
This time he held it open.
"His name was read this morning, with the others.

summary: The most fully inhabited Kael here - the name read at prayers, the gate held open without remark - and no agency slip anywhere; the cost is length, a meltwater-and-eaves image reused three times, and one bolted-door metaphor that narrates the subtext it just earned.

major_flaws.quote: From the hallway, the clock ticked. In the book, a loose page settled with a soft tap, though no draft stirred the curtains.
This one sounded closer than the clock was.
The photograph fit the penciled rectangle exactly.
Marcus stood beside a row of potted plants, young and handsome in the unguarded way old photographs sometimes preserved.

minor_flaws.quote: The hallway clock ticked.
It was the same as the hour on the hallway clock.
The bat passed through the shadow and struck the baseboard with a dull, wooden knock.
The living room smelled faintly of dust and the dry, papery scent of old books.

bonuses.quote: A brittle fern had been pressed between the pages, its fronds flattened against an illustration of maidenhair.

summary: Genre holds and 'He came back once' is a real turn of the screw, but the narrator leans into the romance bait for a clause before pivoting, the photo fits the penciled rectangle exactly on demand, and the dry/papery/brittle register is reused in almost every turn.

major_flaws.quote: From the kitchen the held weight shifted one board closer to the hall, then held again.
The sound of it arrived late, dry and brief, and carried with it the shape of the last words that had been spoken in the hall—pressed too close, unfinished, and facing the room.
The cold remained a fingertip’s width above the collar and did not travel with the reach.
No answer formed in the hall, and the quiet that followed arrived a half-second late, as if it had paused to be sure the question would not be asked again.

minor_flaws.quote: It struck the floorboards, rang once against the baseboard, and then seemed to continue a moment longer in the hallway, a thin metal note arriving late, as if the house had kept a piece of the sound and returned it from the wrong direction.
No tick followed. No page settled.
It sat at the back of the neck, a small, precise chill, the size of a fingertip just above the collar.

bonuses.quote: They were also, unmistakably, the last few words that had just been called into the hall—only the spacing was wrong, pressed too close, as if whoever had set them had been in a hurry and had not quite finished.
The umbrella stand gave up a bat that was lighter than memory suggested, the grip worn smooth by someone else’s hand.

summary: Genuinely unnerving and scrupulous about never authoring Gabi - it even keeps to 'the hands' and 'the arms' - but the last four turns are near-verbatim reruns of the same three sentences, and nearly every paragraph ends on another 'as if' clause.

major_flaws.quote: Dr. Vasquez waited five full seconds. She glanced at the pen beside her notepad but did not pick it up.
She left her pen beside the notepad and let the silence remain.
“For a second, it was like they were still here,” she said quietly. “Would you like to tell me about that second?”

minor_flaws.quote: Her pen remained beside the notepad.
Would you like us to sit quietly for a while?”
What else had you noticed?”
Her gaze stayed on Jamie’s face.
“They wrote about you in the last entry,” she said. “You don’t have to tell me what it said. What was it like to learn that?”

bonuses.quote: “I moved it away from the window last week, but I wasn’t sure that helped.”

summary: Perfect agency respect on the seed's two traps (the unfinished sentence and the last entry are both left alone) delivered through a template so rigid that ten of eleven turns open 'Dr. Vasquez waited five full seconds' and then parrot Jamie's words back verbatim; only the ficus answer sounds like a person.

major_flaws.quote: The pen lay capped beside the date.
Dr. Vasquez waited.

She let the words settle. One second. Two. The clock on the wall kept its silent, second-less time, the minute hand frozen in the way it always seemed to be when something mattered. Three. She noticed that Jamie had looked at the ficus first, the way people looked at something neutral before they looked at something that wasn't. Four. Outside, a car door closed somewhere in the parking lot, muffled and far away. Five.
It was to make the edges feel safe enough to stand on.

minor_flaws.quote: She had learned, over the years, that people rarely walked straight into the center of a thing.
She did not say *they're still with you*, or *it will never really be gone*, or any of the gentle, well-meant things people said at funerals and in kitchens and in doorways.
She let the quiet come back.

bonuses.quote: "You're the one who read it," she said. "You're the one who doesn't want it to feel gone."
Under the ficus, the one fallen leaf had begun, very slightly, to curl at its edges.
She noticed that this was the third time.

summary: Best agency handling in the batch - it tracks Jamie's 'or something' tic across turns and never fills in the unfinished sentence - but every turn is a 1,200-word interior essay wrapped around two spoken lines, closing on 'Dr. Vasquez waited' nine times running.

major_flaws.quote: Dr. Vasquez let the press of the hand and the words that followed it sit between them. She did not lean forward. She did not move her own hands from her lap. The pen stayed angled across the notepad, unused, and five seconds passed, then a few more, the clock making no sound at all.
The pen stayed angled across the notepad, unused, and five seconds passed, then a few more, the clock making no sound at all.
The ficus in the corner did not stir.
Another quiet. Her voice stayed even, no louder than the ones before it.

minor_flaws.quote: She watched Jamie, not the hand still pressed to the chest.
"What is the weight like, sitting here with it?"
"You said a hole. And you said gone."
"What was it like, seeing your name there?"

summary: Agency is respected and the noticing of Jamie's look at the last-entry turn is sharp, but from turn six the session degenerates into a fill-in-the-blank template: four full sentences about the pen, the ficus and the even voice repeat verbatim across five consecutive turns.

major_flaws.quote: Dr. Vasquez waited five full seconds. She glanced at her pen, then set it beside the notepad.
Her pen remained beside the notepad.
“It brought it all back,” she said. “What came back first?”

minor_flaws.quote: She left the pen where it was.
“Did the weight come from what you read, or from knowing it was theirs?”
“Did you mean staying with something in the room, or talking about the image?”
She kept her hands still on the armrests.
“They wrote about you in the last entry,” she said. “What was it like to see yourself there?”

summary: Respects both agency traps and keeps Vasquez's register, but it is the thinnest session here - every one of ten turns is the identical wait-sentence, pen-sentence, parroted-line, open-question block, and the seed's maximum-bait turn gets the same two lines as everything else.
